concept.name: Drawdown
concept.definition: The decline in the value of an account, portfolio, or strategy from a historical peak to a subsequent point before a new peak is reached, typically expressed as a percentage of the peak value. Formally, for an equity process X(t), the drawdown at time T is the running maximum of X up to T minus X(T).
concept.intuition: It is the pain an investor endures between equity highs: how much of the peak value is given back before the account recovers.
concept.mechanics: Track the running maximum of the equity (NAV) series and at each point compute (peak - current) / peak. The series of these values forms the drawdown (underwater) curve, whose extreme values and durations define the maximum drawdown and drawdown duration statistics.
concept.formula: D(T) = max_{t in (0,T)} X(t) - X(T); in percentage terms, DD%(T) = ( max_{t in (0,T)} X(t) - X(T) ) / max_{t in (0,T)} X(t).
concept.failure_modes: Drawdown is path- and sample-dependent: a different evaluation window changes every value, and one deep event dominates the statistic. For illiquid strategies, smoothed or stale marks flatter reported drawdowns.
concept.misconceptions: A drawdown is not a realized loss — positions need not be closed and the account can recover — and the deepest drawdown is not necessarily the longest-lived one.
concept.example: An account that peaks at $120,000 and falls to $96,000 before recovering is in a drawdown of $24,000, or 20% from peak.
